---
title: "CRYSTAL input and output field guide"
---

CRYSTAL input files can become complex, but the first Mineral Science
calculation needs only a small subset of that language.

The objective is **not** to memorize keywords. It is to recognize which part of
the scientific model a keyword controls.

## The input blocks used in Laboratory 2

A useful mental map is:

```text
STRUCTURE
    periodicity
    space group
    cell parameters
    independent atoms

BASIS SET
    Gaussian basis used for the atomic orbitals

DFT
    exchange-correlation functional

NUMERICAL CONTROL
    integral thresholds
    SCF energy convergence
    reciprocal-space sampling
```

The distributed MgO input uses:

```text
BASISSET
POB-TZVP-REV2
```

and:

```text
DFT
PBE
END
```

The reciprocal-space sampling is controlled by:

```text
SHRINK
2 2
```

In Laboratory 2, only the two values following `SHRINK` are changed.

## What to recognize in the output

### Sampling

CRYSTAL prints a line similar to:

```text
SHRINK. FACT.(MONKH.) ... NUMBER OF K POINTS IN THE IBZ ...
```

This gives both the Monkhorst sampling and the number of k-points that remain
after symmetry reduction to the irreducible Brillouin zone.

### SCF cycles

During the self-consistent field procedure CRYSTAL prints lines beginning with:

```text
CYC
```

These contain the current total energy and the change with respect to the
previous cycle.

### Successful SCF convergence

For this laboratory the parser requires a line containing:

```text
SCF ENDED - CONVERGENCE ON ENERGY
```

The final energy printed on that line is the value analysed in the notebook.

### Timing

Near the end of a normal calculation, CRYSTAL reports:

```text
END ... TELAPSE ... TCPU ...
```

`TELAPSE` is the wall-clock time experienced by the calculation.

`TCPU` is accumulated CPU time. With parallel execution, CPU time and elapsed
time are not expected to be identical.

### Normal termination

A complete run ends with a termination marker. The course parser checks this
as well as SCF convergence.

## If an output is incomplete

Do not copy the last visible energy into your results table.

An interrupted calculation may contain several perfectly plausible SCF energy
values without having reached the requested convergence. Keep the output and
inspect the error rather than treating it as a result.
